messages.subject: zero-inflated models
parts:
Hi INLA experts,


I have the following model structure:

Y(i) ~Bin(Ntrial, p(i))

p(i)=p_a + (1-p_a)*prob(i)

logit(prob(i))=alpha + beta* x(i)

I would like to estimate alpha, beta and p_a

After simulating data I have tried to estimate these parameters using the zeroinflated.binomial.1 likelihood (see R code below ). However the 95%CrI do not include the original parameter estimates. Is there an alternative approach I should be using in INLA?


#####################################################################

x1=rep(1:200,20)

n=length(x1)

beta=-0.1

alpha=1.2

eta=rnorm(length(x1),x1*beta+alpha,sd=0.005)


prob=exp(eta)/(1+exp(eta))


p=0.2


pp=p+(1-p)*prob

plot(pp)


y=rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = pp)


data = list(y=y,x1=x1)

formula = y ~ 1+x1

  

 

result1 = inla(formula, family = "zeroinflatedbinomial1", data = data, Ntrials=rep(1,n))

summary(result1)

#######################################################################

I would also like to extend this approach such that:


Y(i,j) ~Bin(Ntrial, p(i,j))

p(i,j)=[p_a + (1-p_a)*prob(i)] * p_rand(j)

logit(prob(i))=alpha + beta* x(i)

logit(p_rand(j)) ~Norm(0,sigma_j)


Is this possible? I would like to use INLA as the real data I would like to fit to has a hierarchical structure and I would like to include several spatial and temporal random effects.

 

Any help is much appreciated,

Many thanks,

Isobel
